A mothman has a unique relationship with fate and destiny, and while they are generally solitary, one often appears before large natural disasters.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly - Cryptids p. 22 (Third Party)

fields.name: Sasquatch

trait.name: Spellcasting
trait.text:
The sasquatch can cast the following spells without requiring material components using Wisdom as its spellcasting ability (spell save DC 13, spell attack bonus +5).

	• At will: entangle, pass without trace, speak with plants
	• 3/day Each: freedom of movement, grasping vine, hallucinatory terrain, tree stride

trait.name: Strength of the Wild
trait.text: The sasquatch has advantage on Strength checks and saving throws.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The sasquatch makes two club attacks.

action.name: Club
action.text: Melee weapon attack: +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 14 (2d8+5) bludgeoning damage. If the target is a creature of huge size or smaller, it is knocked prone.

action.name: Ground Pound
action.text: The sasquatch slams its fist on the ground, creating a powerful shockwave. Creatures on the ground within 30 ft. of the sasquatch must make DC 13 Constitution saving throws. On a failure, creatures suffer 14 (2d8+5) thunder damage and are knocked prone. On a success, the creature takes half damage and is not knocked prone.

fields.spells: Entangle, Pass Without Trace, Speak with Plants, Freedom of Movement, Grasping Vine, Hallucinatory Terrain, Tree Stride
fields.description:
A sasquatch is a powerfully built, broad-shouldered humanoid figure covered in shaggy hair, with long, muscular arms, giving it an overall ape-like appearance. They live in isolated, small family groups in wild settings, as far from civilization as possible, and they often work with druidic circles to protect the beauty of nature.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly - Cryptids p. 23 (Third Party)

fields.name: Thinman

trait.name: Psychic Disturbance Field
trait.text: The thinman projects an area of psychic disturbance. Creatures starting their turn within 30 ft. of the thinman must make DC 15 Intelligence saving throws or suffer disadvantage on attack rolls, saving throws, and ability checks until the start of the thinman's next turn. The thinman can disable or enable this aura as a bonus action.

trait.name: Thin Form
trait.text: Thinman can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch wide without squeezing.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The thinman makes three tendril attacks.

action.name: Tendril
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (1d8+5) bludgeoning damage and 13 (3d8) psychic damage.

action.name: Sprout Tendrils
action.text: The thinman casts black tentacles (DC 15) without requiring material components.

action.name: Ego Collapse
action.text: The thinman targets one creature within 60 ft. The target must make a DC 15 Intelligence saving throw. On a failed save, the target takes 36 (8d8) psychic damage and is blinded and deafened for 1 minute. On a success, the target takes half damage and suffers no additional effects.

action.name: Bodily Transformation (Bonus Action)
action.text: The thinman can teleport up to 60 ft. to an unoccupied space it can see. It can pass through solid objects while doing so, but it cannot end its movement inside an object.

fields.description:
Faceless and tall, a thinman has pale skin beneath an exterior layer of sleek black slime, formed into a mockery of civilized clothing. Tendrils of its inky black exterior stretch out from its back, extending its already formidable reach. These creatures originate from another plane of existence, and their wants and desires are completely unknown.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly - Cryptids p. 24 (Third Party)

fields.name: Pseudo Hydra

trait.name: Magic Resistance
trait.text: The pseudo hydra has advantage on saving throws against spells and spell-like effects.

trait.name: Spellcasting
trait.text:
The pseudo hydra can cast the following spells without requiring material components using Wisdom as its spellcasting ability (spell save DC 16, spell attack bonus +8). The pseudo hydra can concentrate on up to four spell at once.

	• At will: Fear, invisibility, major image, modify memory.
	• 3/day each: Dream, mirage arcane, seeming
	• 1/day each: Weird

trait.name: Spider Climb
trait.text: The pseudo hydra can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability heck.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The pseudo hydra makes four bite attacks. It can replace one of its bite attacks with an At Will spell from its Spellcasting feature.

action.name: Bite
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +11 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (1d12+7) piercing damage plus 6 (1s12) psychic damage.

fields.spells: Fear, Invisibility, Major Image, Modify Memory., Dream, Mirage Arcane, Seeming, Weird
fields.description:
A psuedo hydra appears as a mass of pale, writhing, worm-like appendages sprouting from a central formless body. Some appendages end in long claws while others hold the hovering visage of a hollow-eyed face, mouths open at grotesque angles.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly - Cryptids p. 26 (Third Party)

fields.name: Water Orm
fields.resist: bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks, cold

trait.name: Amphibious
trait.text: The water orm can breathe both air and water.

trait.name: Aquatic Ambusher
trait.text: The water orm has advantage on initiative checks while in the water.

trait.name: Slippery
trait.text: While in the water, the water orm can use its bonus action to take the Dash, Disengage, or Dodge action.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The water orm makes two bite attacks and performs a water blast.

action.name: Bite
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 16 (2d10+5) piercing damage.

action.name: Water Blast
action.text: The water orm releases a blast of water in a 60-foot line. Creatures in the line must make DC 15 Strength saving throws or be pushed back 15 feet.

fields.description: Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly - Cryptids p. 27 (Third Party)

fields.name: Alraune
fields.resist: Psychic, bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.

trait.name: Alluring Scent
trait.text: Creatures that enter or start their turn within 30 ft. of the alraune must make a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw or be charmed by the alraune for 1 minute. A creature charmed in this way only can move as close as it can to the alraune. A creature charmed by the alraune can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. Creatures that have succeeded on this saving throw are immune to the alraune's alluring scent for 24 hours.

trait.name: Innate Spellcasting
trait.text:
The Alraune's innate spellcasting ability is Charisma (spell save DC 15). It can innately cast the following spells with no material components. 

	• At will: druidcraft, minor illusion, charm person.
	• 3/day each: entangle, suggestion, phantasmal force
	• 1/day each: plant growth, dominate person

trait.name: Plant camouflage
trait.text: The alraune has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks it makes in areas of dense foliage.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The alraune attacks twice with constrict.

action.name: Constrict
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d6 + 3) bludgeoning and an additional 4 (1d6) piercing damage. Large or smaller creatures must make a DC 16 Str (Athletics) check when they are hit or be restrained. They may repeat this save as an action on their turn.
action.attack: Bludgeoning And An Additional 4 (1d6) Piercing Damage|+6|1d6+3

action.name: Vampiric Vines
action.text: The Alraune causes thorny vines to erupt from the ground in a 20foot radius centered on itself. Each creature of its choice in the area must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking 27 (6d8) necrotic damage on a failed saave, or half as much on a success. The alraune regains hit points equal to half the total damage dealt.

fields.spells: Druidcraft, Minor Illusion, Charm Person, Entangle, Suggestion, Phantasmal Force, Plant Growth, Dominate Person
fields.description:
Alraune's are plant-fey hybrids born from cursed soil, taking the form of alluring humanoid flowers that ensnare the hearts and minds of the living. They lure intruders with intoxicating pheromones and then drain vitality to feed their ever-hungry roots.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly - Fantastic Flora p. 14 (Third Party)

fields.name: Aureolin Musk Creeper

trait.name: False Appearance
trait.text: While motionless, this creature is indistinguishable from a benign plant.

trait.name: Regeneration
trait.text: The creeper regains 15 hit points at the start of its turn. If it takes fire, necrotic, or radiant damage, this trait doesn't function at the start of the creeper's next turn. The creeper dies only if it starts its turn with 0 hit points and cannot regenerate.

action.name: Vines
action.text: Melee weapon attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 14 (4d6) piercing damage. If the target is a humanoid or beast that drops to 0 hit points as a result of this damage, it is implanted with an aureolin musk creeper bulb. Creatures implanted with a bulb are poisoned until the bulb is removed. The bulb is destroyed by a remove curse or restoration spell. Dead bulb-implanted creatures revive after 24 hours as aureolin musk creepers.

action.name: Aureolin Musk
action.text: The creeper's flowers release an irrating musk that targets all humanoids and beasts within 30 ft. of it. Each target must succeed on a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw or become enraged for 1 minute. An enraged creature must spend its turn moving to be adjacent to the nearest other humanoid or beast, dashing if necessary, and then attacking with a mele attack. A creature enraged by the creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of its of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. Creatures that are immune to being charmed cannot be affected by the musk.

fields.description:
A dangerous, vine-like plant that exudes a sweet, intoxicating musk to lure living creatures close. Once ensnared, it implants spores that slowly turn victims into mindless thralls, spreading its tending the monstrous flora.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly - Fantastic Flora p. 16 (Third Party)

fields.name: Aureolin Musk Zombie

trait.name: Enraged Zombie Fortitude
trait.text: If damage reduces the zombie to 0 hit points, it must make a Constitution saving throw with a DC equal to the damage taken, unless the damage is fire or is a critical hit. On a success, the zombie drops to 1 hit point instead.

trait.name: Aureolin Musk Death Cloud
trait.text: When the zombie dies, its flowers release an irritating musk that targets all humanoids and beasts within 30 ft. of it. Each target must succeed on a DC 10 Wisdom saving throw or become enraged for 1 minute. An enraged creature must spend its turns moving to be adjacent to the nearest other humanoid or beast and attacking. An enraged creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of its of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. Creatures that are immune to being charmed cannot be affected by the musk.

action.name: Slam
action.text: Melee weapon attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 9 (1d8+4) bludgeoning damage.

fields.description:
The juvenile form of the aureolin musk creeper. A corpse covered in sprawling, sickly vines and covered in yellow blossoms, exuding a reeking pollen. The creatures stumble forward seeking to spread the yellow musk pollen far and wide.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly - Fantastic Flora p. 17 (Third Party)

fields.name: Flowering Shambling Mound

trait.name: False Appearance
trait.text: While motionless, this creature is indistinguishable from a benign plant.

trait.name: Lightning Absorption
trait.text: Whenever the flowering shambling mound is hit with lightning damage, it takes no damage and regains a number of hit points equal to the lightning damage taken.

trait.name: Irritating Pollen
trait.text: When damaged by an attack, creatures within 10 ft. of the flowering shambling mound must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or become poisoned for one round.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The flowering shambling mound makes two slam attacks.

action.name: Slam
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (2d8+4) bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Cloud of Pollen
action.text: Creatures within 30 ft. of the flowering shamblin mound must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or become stunned for one round and take 14 (4d6) poison damage.

fields.description:
Once a shambling mound has existed for a few months, new seedlings begin to grow that reinforce the electrified dead vegetation. This new life makes the shambling mound more aggressive, especially as the plants begin to flower.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly - Fantastic Flora p. 18 (Third Party)

fields.name: Mandrake

trait.name: False Appearance
trait.text: While motionless, this creature is indistinguishable from a benign plant.

action.name: Slam
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +4, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d4+2) bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Scream
action.text: All creatures that are not plants in a 15 ft. cone must make a DC 12 Constitution saving throw or take 11 (3d6) thunder damage and become stunned for 1 turn on a failed saving throw, taking half damage on a success.

fields.description:
Mandrakes are small, root-like plant creatures that resemble ugly and wrinkled human infants with leafy green shoots sprouting from their heads. Though slow and harmless on their own, they emit a piercing screech when disturbed, startling predators and alerting nearby allies. Herbalists prize them for their magical properties, but harvesting one without proper care can trigger its shriek, drawing unwanted attention.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly - Fantastic Flora p. 19 (Third Party)

fields.name: Nepenthes Mantrap

trait.name: False Appearance
trait.text: While motionless, this creature is indistinguishable from a benign plant.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The nepenthese mantrap makes two vine lash attacks.

action.name: Vine Lash
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d8+2) bludgeoning damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 13 Strength saving throw or be grappled (escape DC 13). Until this grapple ends, the target is restrained and the mantrap can't use that vine on another target.

action.name: Engulf
action.text: The nepenthese mantrap attempts to swallow a Medium or smaller creature it has grappled. The creature must succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw or be pulled inside the mantrap's flower. While engulfed, the creature is blinded and restrained, has total cover against attacks, and other effects outside the Mantrap, and takes 5 (2d4) acid damage at the start of each of the mantrap's turns. A creature can attempt to escape by succeeding on a DC 13 Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check as an action.

fields.description:
The majority of the size of this carnivorous pitcher plant is the large acid-filled pitcher. With a sweet aroma and a hunger for prey this plant makes a great addition to any garden with too many pests.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly - Fantastic Flora p. 20 (Third Party)

fields.name: Primeval Wood Woad

trait.name: Innate Spellcasting
trait.text:
The primeval wood woad's spellcasting ability is Wisdom (spell save DC 13). The wood woad can innately cast spells without material components.

	• Cantrips (at will): Druid Craft, Thorn Whip
	• 1st level (3 slots): Entangle, Pass without Trace

trait.name: Magic Club
trait.text: In the primeval wood woad's hand, its club is magical and deals 4 (2d4) extra damage included in its attacks.

trait.name: Plant Camouflage
trait.text: The primeval wood woad has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks it makes in areas of dense foliage.

trait.name: Regeneration
trait.text: The primeval wood woad regains 10 hit points at the start of its turn if it is in contact with the ground. If it takes fire, necrotic, or radiant damage, this trait doesn't function at the start of the primeval wood woad's next turn. The primeval wood woad r dies only if it starts its turn with 0 hit points and cannot regenerate.

trait.name: Tree Stride
trait.text: Once on its turn, the primeval wood woad can use 10 ft. of its movement to step magically into one living tree within reach and emerge from a second living tree within 50 ft. of the first tree appearing in an unoccupied space within 5 ft. of the second tree. Both trees must be Large or bigger.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
trait.text: The primeval wood woad has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Speak with Plants
trait.text: The primeval wood woad can communicate with plants as if they shared a language.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The primeval wood woad makes two attacks with its club.

action.name: Club
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (3d4+3) bludgeoning damage.

fields.spells: Druid Craft, Thorn Whip, Entangle, Pass without Trace
fields.description:
An ancient and gnarled version of a wood woad, these plants take centuries to reach full maturity. They cannot grow in urban environments and must have a minimum of one mile of dense forest per wood woad.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly - Fantastic Flora p. 22 (Third Party)

fields.name: Slithering Assassin Vine

trait.name: False Appearance
trait.text: While motionless, this creature is indistinguishable from a benign plant.

trait.name: Damage Transfer
trait.text: While grappling with a creature, the assassin vine takes only half the damage dealt to it (rounded down), and the grappled creature takes the other half.

action.name: Constrict
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (2d6+4) bludgeoning damage, and if the target is large or smaller, it and the assassin vine become grappled. While grappled, the assassin vine can make this attack only against its grappled target and has advantage on the attack roll. The assassin vine can detach itself by spending 5 feet of its movement. A creature, including the target, can take its action to detach the assassin vine by succeeding on a DC 16 Str (Athletics) check. At the end of each of the grappled creature's turns they must succeed on a DC 14 Constitution saving throw or begin to suffocate.

action.name: Bulb
action.text: Bulb can only be used on a creature the assassin vine is grappling.  Target must make a DC 16 Constitution saving throw. On a failure, they take 16 (3d8+4) slashing damage and a small bulb is injected under their skin. During the creature's next long rest the bulb grows into another slithering assassin vine that starts attached to the target. The new assassin vine lacks this ability for one month. The bulb can be removed with a DC 16 Wisdom (Medicine) check.

fields.description:
This mobile constricting vine suffocates prey by wrapping around the target's head and neck. The adult slithering assassin uses friction to cut open skin, placing a bulb beneath the surface.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly - Fantastic Flora p. 24 (Third Party)

fields.name: Snapping Bloom

trait.name: False Appearance
trait.text: While motionless, this creature is indistinguishable from a benign plant.

trait.name: Blood Meal
trait.text: This creature gets advantage on attack rolls against creatures that are at or below half health.

trait.name: Powerful Jaws
trait.text: This creature ignores resistance to piercing damage.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The snapping bloom makes a bite attack and then a reel attack.

action.name: Bite
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 30 ft., one target. Hit: 12 (2d6+5) piercing damage, and the target must make a DC 18 Strength (Athletics) check or be restrained. While it has a creature restrained, the snapping bloom cannot bite another target.

action.name: Reel
action.text: A target creature the snapping bloom has grappled is pulled 10 ft. towards it and takes 14 (2d8+5) piercing damage. If the target ends its movement adjacent to the snapping bloom, it may immediately make a chomp attack.

action.name: Chomp
action.text: The snapping bloom can only perform a Chomp action upon an adjacent medium or smaller creature that is has restrained. Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 30 ft., one target. Hit: 33 (8d6 + 5) piercing damage. On a successful hit, the target is no longer restrained.

fields.description:
A large plant with a prominent bulb-shaped flower resting on a long flexible stalk. These perpetually hungry plants kill their prey with rows of hard teeth like petals at the center of their flower.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly - Fantastic Flora p. 25 (Third Party)

fields.name: Tropical Thorny

trait.name: Plant Camouflage
trait.text: The tropical thorny has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks it makes in areas of dense foliage.

trait.name: Solar Enhancements
trait.text: When in direct sunlight, the thorny has advantage on attack rolls.

trait.name: Solar Regeneration
trait.text: While in direct sunlight, the thorny heals 4 hit points at the start of its turn. If it takes cold, fire or necrotic damage, this trait doesn't function at the start of the thorny's next turn. The thorny only dies if it starts its turn with 0 hit points and doesn't regenerate.

trait.name: Vines
trait.text: The thorny sticks to anything that touches it. A huge or smaller creature that the thorny touches is grappled. While grappled, the creature takes 1d4 piercing damage at the beginning of each of their turns. To escape, the grappled creature must make a DC 12 Strength saving throw at the beginning of its turn.

action.name: Bite
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (2d6+2) piercing damage.

action.name: Thorn Spray
action.text: The thorny spews thorns in a 15 ft. cone. All creatures in the cone must make a DC 12 Dexterity saving throw or take 5 (1d4+2) piercing damage.

action.name: Slam
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (2d4+2) piercing damage. The target must make a DC 12 Strength saving throw or they will be grappled by the vines.

fields.description:
A loyal floral companion if raised from a seedling, this vine-covered quadruped is aggressive towards strangers. If well-taken-care-of, offprint of the tropical thorny are known to recognize those close to their progenitors without ever meeting them.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly - Fantastic Flora p. 26 (Third Party)

fields.name: Tropical Vegepygmy

trait.name: Plant Camouflage
trait.text: The tropical vegepygmy has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks in areas of dense foliage.

trait.name: Hardened
trait.text: The tropical vegepygmy takes no falling damage.

trait.name: Solar Enhancement
trait.text: While in direct sunlight, the vegepygmy gets advantage on attack rolls. Additionally, damage from the plummet action deals an additional 1d6 radiant damage and ignores bludgeoning resistance.

trait.name: Solar Regeneration
trait.text: While in direct sunlight, the vegepygmy heals 4 hit points at the start of its turn. if it takes cold, fire or necrotic damage, this trait doesn't function at the start of the vegepygmy's next turn. The vegepygmy dies only if it starts its turn with 0 hit points and doesn't regenerate.

action.name: Claw
action.text: Melee weapon attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. hit: 5 (1d4+2) slashing damage.

action.name: Plummet
action.text: The vegepygmy targets a creature at least 10 feet directly below it and drops down. The target must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or take 1d6 bludgeoning damage for every 10 feet fallen (maximum 3d6). If in direct sunlight, the attack deals an additional 1d6 radiant damage and ignores bludgeoning resistance.

fields.description:
These small intelligent creatures are covered in a hard coconut-like shell. Their aggression towards outsiders makes them difficult for gardeners to grow.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly - Fantastic Flora p. 28 (Third Party)

fields.name: Avalanche Giant

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The gaint makes two slam attacks or two iceberg attacks.

action.name: Slam
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +11 to hit, range 10 ft., one target. Hit: 14 (1d12+7) bludgeoning damage and 4 (1d6) cold damage. Creatures that are medium or smaller that are hit with this attack must succeed on a DC 15 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone.

action.name: Iceberg
action.text: Ranged weapon attack: +11 to hit, range 60/240 ft., one target. Hit: 14 (2d6+7) bludgeoning damage and the target must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw. On a failure, the target becomes restrained. On a success, the target's movement speed is reduced by 10 ft. This effect last until the start of the target's next turn.

action.name: Charge
action.text:
The avalanche giant moves in a straight line up to 60 ft. moving through the space of any enemies that are large or smaller, or stopping when it hits any impassable terrain. Any creature whose space was moved through must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, the creature takes 21 (3d8+7) bludgeoning damage and is pushed in the same direction 20 ft. past where the avalanche giant ended its movement. 
	If a creature pushed in this way would collide with a stationary object, it takes an additional 13 (3d8) bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Ice Barrier
action.text: The avalanche giant casts wall of ice at 6th level with a DC 15 spell saving throw.

fields.description:
The living embodiment of a mountainside's wrath, these titanic beings stride with the force of landslides, burying intruders beneath boulders and sheets of crushing frost. Territorial and near-mindless, they are living disasters driven by ancient instincts to protect the high peaks from the touch of civilization.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly - Legends of Norse Mythology p. 14 (Third Party)

fields.name: Draugr
fields.languages: understands all languages it spoke in life but can't speak

trait.name: Stench
trait.text: Any creature that starts its turn within 10 ft. of the draugr must succeed on a DC 9 Constitution saving throw or become poisoned until the start of its next turn. On a success, the creature is immune to the draugr's stench for 24 hours.

trait.name: Corpselike
trait.text: While motionless, the draugr is indistinguishable from a normal corpse.

trait.name: Resurrecting
trait.text: If the corpse of a draugr is not dealt radiant or fire damage, it will return to life with full hit points at the next sundown.

action.name: Spear
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d6+2) piercing damage and 3 (1d4) cold damage.

action.name: Evil Eye
action.text: The draugr states with its evil eye at a creature it can see within 60 ft. The creature must succeed on a DC 9 Charisma saving throw or take 3 (1d4) necrotic damage and have disadvantage on attack rolls and saving throws until the end of its next turn.

fields.description:
Guarding the wealth of cairns and royal tombs, draugr are reanimated corpses. Their frostbitten and weathered skin is inured to the cold.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly - Legends of Norse Mythology p. 16 (Third Party)

fields.name: Lava Giant

trait.name: Fumarole Cloak
trait.text: Creatures that enter or begin their turn within 10 ft. of the lava giant must succeed on a DC 14 Constitution saving throw or take 7 (2d6) poison damage and 7 (2d6) fire damage. Creatures farther than 30 ft. from the lava giant have disadvantage on ranged attack rolls against it.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The giant uses its battleaxe attack and then its rock attack.

action.name: Battleaxe
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, range 10 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (3d6+6) slashing damage plus 4 (1d6) fire damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 17 Strength saving throw or be pushed back 30 ft. The lava giant may choose to ignore this secondary effect.

action.name: Rock
action.text: Ranged Weapon Attack: +9, range 60/240 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (3d6+6) bludgeoning damage. All creatures within 5 ft. of the target, including the target, must succeed on a DC 14 Dexterity saving throw or take 14 (4d6) fire damage. This effect occurs even if the original attack misses.

action.name: Lava Stomp
action.text: The giant stomps the ground. All creatures within 30 ft. must succeed on a DC 14 Dexterity saving throw or take 21 (6d6) fire damage. The ground affected by this attack remains molten for 3 rounds, becoming difficult terrain and dealing 7 (2d6) fire damage to all creatures for each 5 ft. of movement they make across the molten ground. A 5 ft. square of heated ground can be cooled prematurely by dealing at least 1 cold damage or by using a gallon of water.

fields.description:
Lava giants are mighty, flame-wreathed warriors born in the hearts of volcanoes and forged by the wrath of forgotten fire gods. The skin is red-hot, and every strike of their runed axes spits great globs of molten rock. They guard the sacred volcanic forges of the old world, testing all who trespass with trials of fire and fury.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly - Legends of Norse Mythology p. 17 (Third Party)

fields.name: Grendel
fields.immune: bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks, fire, cold

trait.name: Sensitive Hearing
trait.text: Whenever the grendel takes thunder damage, it has disadvantage on attack rolls until the end of the next round.

trait.name: Nocturnal Stealth
trait.text: While in darkness, the grendel is invisible. While in dim light, the grendel has +10 bonus to Dexterity (Stealth) checks.

trait.name: Sneak Attack
trait.text: If the grendel has advantage on an attack roll, it adds 2d6 to the damage of that attack.

trait.name: Stalker
trait.text: The grendel has +10 bonus to Wisdom (Survival) checks made to track and follow prey.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The grendel makes three attacks: two with its claws and one with its bite.

action.name: Claw
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 19 (3d8+5) slashing damage.

action.name: Bite
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 19 (3d8+5) piercing damage. If the target is a beast or humanoid, the grendel regains a number of hit points equal to the damage dealt.

action.name: Raging Throw
action.text: One creature within 5 ft. must make a DC 17 Strength saving throw. On a failure, the creature is thrown 40 ft. and takes 23 (4d8+5) bludgeoning damage. If the creature collides with another target within range, that target must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or take 23 (4d8+5) bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Frightful Presence
action.text: Each creature of the grendel's choice within 60 ft. that is aware of it must succeed ona. DC 14 Wisdom saving throw or become frightened of the grendel for 1 minute.  A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. Once the effect ends for a creature, it is immune to the grendel's Frightful Presence for the next 24 hours.

action.name: Snuff Flame (Bonus Action)
action.text: The grendel extinguishes a single source of fire within 20 ft. no larger than a 5 ft. cube.

action.name: Gorge (Bonus Action)
action.text: The grendel consumes a corpse and regain 18 (4d8) hit points.

fields.description:
A grendel is a monstrous, solitary predator born from cursed bloodlines and ancient vengeance, lurking at the edges of civilization where wild darkness endures. Towering and sinewy, with mottled flesh like wet stone and claws that rend armor like cloth, it emerges only to slaughter, drawn by joyless hunger and the sound of revelry. Shunned by even other monsters, grendels are the bane of. halls and hearths.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly - Legends of Norse Mythology p. 18 (Third Party)

fields.name: Huldra

trait.name: Forest Dweller
trait.text: The huldra has advantage on any Intelligence (History), Intelligence (Nature), or Wisdom (Survival) checks made about the forest they inhabit.

trait.name: Speak with Beasts
trait.text: The huldra can communicate with beasts as if they shared a language.

trait.name: Underbrush Walker
trait.text: Wisdom (Survival) checks made to track the huldra have disadvantage.

action.name: Claw
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d4+3) slashing damage.

action.name: Irresistible Dance
action.text: The huldra can cast irresistible dance with a spell save DC of 13.

action.name: Charming
action.text: Target creature that can see the huldra must make a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw or become charmed for 1 minute. The creature may repeat this save at the end of each of its turns, or whenever they take damage.

fields.description:
Huldra are hauntingly beautiful forest wardens with bark-lined hearts and hollowed wooden spines, cloaked to conceal the truth of their nature. born of old primal magic and shaped by human longing, they offer aid and shelter to those who respect the wild places.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly - Legends of Norse Mythology p. 20 (Third Party)

fields.name: Lindworm
fields.languages: Draconic, understands Common and Giant but can't speak

trait.name: Old-Blood Resilience
trait.text: The lindworm has advantage on saving throws against poison, and magic can't put it to sleep.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The lindworm makes two attacks: one with its bite and one with its tail.

action.name: Bite
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 15 (2d10+4) piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) poison damage, and the target must then make a DC 11 Constitution saving throw or become paralyzed until the end of the lindworm's next turn.

action.name: Tail Slam
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (2d8+4) bludgeoning damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a DC 15 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone.

action.name: Venomous Spray
action.text: The lindworm sprays its blinding venom in a 15 ft. cone. All creatures within the cone must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw. On a failure, the creature 14 (4d6) poison damage and is blinded for one minute. At the end of each blinded creatures' turn, it can repeat this saving throw, ending the effect on itself on a success. On a success, the creature takes half as much poison damage and isn't blinded.

fields.description:
Lindworms are ancient, serpentine dragons. Lacking wings and hind limbs, they slither through deep caverns and shadowy forests, speaking curses in forgotten tongues and coiling around old cairns and barrows. They strike with venomous fury when disturbed.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly - Legends of Norse Mythology p. 21 (Third Party)

fields.name: Mountain Troll

trait.name: Stony Skin
trait.text: If the troll would take 10 or less damage from an attack, it instead takes no damage.

trait.name: Sunlight Hypersensitivity
trait.text: The troll takes 20 radiant damage when it starts its turn in sunlight. While in sunlight, it has disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks. Additionally, if the troll drops to 0 hit points while in sunlight, it become petrified and cannot regenerate.

trait.name: Regeneration
trait.text: The troll regains 10 hit points at the start of its turn. If the troll takes radiant damage, this trait doesn't function at the start of the troll's next turn. The troll dies only if it starts its turn with 0 hit points and doesn't regenerate.

trait.name: Hatred of Divine
trait.text: The trolls deals an extra 7 (2d6) damage to any creature that casts divine spells (clerics, paladins, druids, etc) or is under the effect of a divine spell or ability (such as bless, divine smite, channel divinity, etc).

trait.name: Divine Sense
trait.text: The troll can sense the presence of divine magic within 30 feet, as if it always had detect evil and good active, but it only registers celestial, cleric/paladin spellcasters, and ongoing divine magic.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The troll makes three attacks: two with its claws and one with its bite.

action.name: Claw
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 12 (2d6+5) piercing damage.

action.name: Bite
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, rach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 16 (2d10+5) piercing damage.

action.name: Alchemical Grabbag
action.text:
The troll reaches into its bag and pulls a potion. Roll a d4 to determine which potion was pulled and then use the potion.

Alchemical Grabbag:
d4 | Potion
1 | Bitter Cure
2 | Stink Bomb
3 | Sticking Mud
4 | Rocks in a Bottle

action.name: Bitter Cure
action.text: The troll takes 4 (1d6) poison damage and then it may make an additional saving throw against an effect of their choice. The troll then heals 7 (2d6).

action.name: Stink Bomb
action.text: A stinking cloud forms at a point within 40 ft. All creatures must succeed on a DC 14 Constitution saving throw or take 5 (1d8) poison damage and become poisoned for 1d6 rounds.

action.name: Sticking Mud
action.text: One creature within 40 ft. of the troll must succeed on a DC 14 Dexterity saving trhrow, or have their AC reduced by 2 for 1 minute. This effect does not stack.

action.name: Rocks in a Bottle
action.text: Ranged Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, range 40/80 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage.

fields.description:
Smarter than their common brethren, mountain trolls have a semblance of society, and some are even willing to trade, especially for goods found above ground - as they turn to stone if they enter sunlight. In exchange, they are willing to part with the strange potions they create. These creatures are known to wear simple clothing and have an intense hatred for the divine.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly - Legends of Norse Mythology p. 22 (Third Party)

fields.name: Norn
fields.immune: necrotic, psychic, bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks

trait.name: Magical Resistance
trait.text: The norn has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Timeless
trait.text: A norn is immune to effects that would alter its age, perception of time, or ability to act in combat (such as time stop or slow). It can also not be surprised.

trait.name: Norn Coven
trait.text:
Norns are known to work as a trio in a coven. A coven is made up of three norns all of whom are equals within the group. One focuses on the past, another on the present, and the final one on the future. While all three members of a norn coven are within 30 ft. of one another, they gain the following benefits:

	• What Was. If a spell is used by a norm, and the target succeeds on their saving throw and is unaffected, the norn recovers the lost spell slot.

	• What is. The norns are immune to critical hits. Additionally attacks rolls made with their shears critically hit on a 19-20.

	• What Will Be. The duration of cut thread and weave thread increases to 2d4 rounds.

trait.name: Spellcasting
trait.text:
The norn is an 18th level spellcaster. Its spellcasting ability is Wisdom (spell save DC 16, +8 to hit with spell attacks). The norn can cast disguise self at will.

	• Cantrips (at will): Guidance, Resistance, Spare the Dying, Sacred Flame
	• 1st level (4 slots): Bane, Bless, Command, Inflict Wound
	• 2nd level (3 slots): Aid, Augury, Locate Object
	• 3rd level (3 slots): Clairvoyance, Bestow Curse, Dispel Magic
	• 4th level (3 slots): Banishment, Divination, Locate Creature
	• 5th level (3 slots): Geas, Legend Lore, Scrying
	• 6th level (1 slots): Harm
	• 7th level (1 slots): Divine Word
	• 8th level (1 slots): Control Weather
	• 9th level (1 slots): Gate

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The norn makes three attacks with its shears.

action.name: Shears
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (4d6+3) slashing damage plus 9 (2d8) force damage. If the target is below half its hit points maximum, it must succeed on a DC 17 Constitution saving throw or be paralyzed until the end of its next turn.

action.name: Cut Thread
action.text: The norn targets one creature it can see within 30 feet. The creature must make a DC 17 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the target drops to 0 hit points. On a success, it takes 33 (6d10) force damage. This ability has no effect on creatures immune to being frightened.

reaction.name: Bend Fate
reaction.text: Once per round, after a d20 is rolled, but before the effect takes place, the norn may choose to force that d20 to be re-rolled. The original roll is entirely discarded, substituted by the secondary roll.

fields.spells: Disguise Self, Guidance, Resistance, Spare the Dying, Sacred Flame, Bane, Bless, Command, Inflict Wound, Aid, Augury, Locate Object, Clairvoyance, Bestow Curse, Dispel Magic, Banishment, Divination, Locate Creature, Geas, Legend Lore, Scrying, Harm, Divine Word, Control Weather, Gate
fields.description:
Few know the whims of a norn. These creatures who bend fate to their will are just as likely to aid someone as fight them. Prophecies are the only things norns cherish. They often take the form of women at various ages. Those lucky, or unlucky, enough to see them state there is an otherworldliness to the way they look and act that is hard to describe.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly - Legends of Norse Mythology p. 24 (Third Party)

fields.name: Tatzelwurm

trait.name: Coiled Pounce
trait.text: If the tatzelwurm moves at least 20 feet straight toward a creature and then hits it with a claw attack on the same turn, the target must succeed on a DC 13 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone. The tatzelwurm can then make one bite attack against the target as a bonus action

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The tatzelwurm makes two attacks: one with its bite and one with its claws.

action.name: Bite
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (2d6+3) piercing damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or take 5 (2d4) poison damage and be poisoned until the end of its next turn.

action.name: Claw
action.text: Melee Weapon Damage: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (2d4+2) slashing damage.

action.name: Poisonous Breath
action.text: All creatures in a 15 ft. cone must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or become poisoned for 1 minute. A poisoned creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

fields.description:
These cat-faced wurms are known for their headache-inducing breath and pervasive shrieks when on the prowl. Much like the proud and playful hall cat with which they share a face, tatzelwurms can form relationships with other creatures who provide shelter, protection, or conveniently misplaced pieces of meat.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly - Legends of Norse Mythology p. 26 (Third Party)
fields.environment: urban, forest, hill, grassland, desert, swamp

fields.name: Valkyrie
fields.resist: lightning, poison, radiant, bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks

trait.name: Inspiring Leader
trait.text: Allied creatures within 20 ft. of the valkyrie gain a bonus to their saving throws equal to the valkyurie's Charisma modifier.

trait.name: Radiant Armament
trait.text: Any weapon held by the valkyrie becomes a +1 magic weapon that deals an extra 9 (2d8) radiant damage on a hit.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The valkyrie makes two spear attacks.

action.name: Spear
action.text: Melee weapon attack: +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (1d10+6) piercing damage plus 9 (2d8) radiant damage.

action.name: Brilliant Landing
action.text: The valkyrie flies up to 60 ft. landing in an unoccupied space. All creatures within 20 ft. must make a DC 16 Dexterity saving throw, taking 23 (4d8+5) radiant damage and becoming blinded for 2 rounds on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

action.name: Pour Mead (Bonus Action)
action.text: The valkyrie feeds an adjacent creature mead from its mead horn. The target regains 14 (3d8) hit points, and is cured of all exhaustion, curses, diseases, and poisons.

action.name: Shield the Worthy (Bonus Action)
action.text: The valkyrie chooses one creature within 30 feet that she can see. That creature gains resistance to all damage until the start of the valkyrie's next turn.

fields.description:
Clad in chainmail and wielding a spear, these celestial warriors are as much protectors of the living as they are protectors of the dead. They shine brilliantly with radiant light, blinding their foes. These divine beings are known to enter battlefields to ferry the slain to the great beyond. Wherever war rages, valkyries aren't far behind.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly - Legends of Norse Mythology p. 27 (Third Party)

fields.name: Viking Berserker

trait.name: Reckless Attack
trait.text: If the berserker misses its attack, it may re-roll the attack roll once, however attack rolls against the viking have advantage until the beginning of its next turn.

trait.name: Die Hard
trait.text: The first time the berserker would fall to 0 hit points, it falls to 1 hit points instead.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The berserker makes two handaxe attacks.

action.name: Handaxe
action.text: Melee or ranged weapon attack: + 5 to hit, reach 5 ft., or range 20/60 ft. Hit: 7 (1d6+3) slashing damage.

action.name: Raging Flurry
action.text: The berserker may make a melee handaxe attack against a creature within range. If the attack hits the berserker may choose a different creature within range and make a melee handaxe attack against that creature. The berserker may continue to make these attacks until either: an attack misses, or all creatures within range have been attacked and damaged by this berserker. A creature that was hit by this berserker cannot be targeted by this attack again this round.

action.name: Rage (Bonus Action)
action.text: As a bonus action, the berserker can enter a rage, becoming resistant to bludgeoning, piercing and slashing damage, and gaining +2 damage to all attacks. The rage lasts for 1 minute, however, it ends early if the berserker is knocked unconscious, or if its turn ends and it hasn't attacked a hostile creature, or taken damage since its last turn.

fields.description:
First into the battle, berserkers swing with wild abandon. Often without armor and wielding nothing but small axes, these Vikings may seem ill prepared and yet are often the only warriors left standing. The mayhem of blood and violence is so intoxicating to the berserker that they may not even realize they are being wounded.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly - Legends of Norse Mythology p. 28 (Third Party)

fields.name: Viking Skald

action.name: Spear
action.text: Melee weapon attack: +4 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d8+2) piercing damage.

action.name: Sling
action.text: Ranged weapon attack: +4 to hit, range 30/120 ft. Hit: 5 (1d4+2) slashing damage.

action.name: Warcry
action.text: One allied creature may use its reaction to make a single weapon attack.

action.name: Healing Verse (Bonus Action)
action.text: One creature of the skald's choice within 30 ft. regains 7 (2d6) hit points.

action.name: Heroic Edda (Bonus Action)
action.text: All allies within 20 ft. reroll 1's and 2's on damage die until the beginning of the skald's next turn.

fields.description:
The bards of viking culture recite heroic poems, even on the battlefield. Warriors are inspired by their words and surge into battle alongside them. They sing and chant in between strikes of their weapons, predicting the mighty blows of their allies.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly - Legends of Norse Mythology p. 29 (Third Party)

fields.name: Viking Jarl

trait.name: Die Hard
trait.text: When the jarl is reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright, it can drop to 1 hit point instead.

trait.name: Grit
trait.text: Whenever the Jarl fails a saving throw it may re-roll the save, however it subtracts 1d4 from the new saving throw. The Jarl must take the second roll.

trait.name: Heroic Leadership
trait.text: When the Jarl or a creature targeted by the Jarl's Command defeats an enemy, all allies within 60 ft. gain 1d4 temporary hit points.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The Jarl makes two greataxe attacks and two longbow attacks.

action.name: Greataxe
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (1d12+4) slashing damage. On a critical hit, the target must succeed on a DC 16 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone.

action.name: Longbow
action.text: Ranged Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, range 150/600 ft. Hit: 7 (1d8+2) piercing damage.

action.name: Command (Bonus Action)
action.text: One allied creature that can hear the Jarl and has a CR or level below 8 may make a single weapon attack with advantage against a creature of the Jarl's choice within range of the attack.

action.name: March Order (Bonus Action)
action.text: Up to 8 creatures of the Jarl's choice within 60 ft. may immediately move up to 30 ft.

action.name: Brace Order (Bonus Action)
action.text: Up to 8 creatures of the Jarl's choice within 60 ft. may choose to have their speed reduced to 0 and gain +3 to their AC until the beginning of the Jarl's next turn.

fields.description:
The survivor of hundreds of battles, the Jarl is the leader of Viking villages. With age comes wisdom and the ability to lead, along with the grit and determination to survive in such a harsh environment.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly - Legends of Norse Mythology p. 30 (Third Party)

fields.name: World Serpent
fields.languages: understands Draconic and Celestial, but doesn't speak
fields.immune: cold, poison, bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks
fields.conditionImmune: charmed, poisoned, exhaustion, frightened, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, prone

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
trait.text: If the World Serpent fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Eater of Worlds
trait.text: The World Serpent can breathe underwater, walk on water, and is immune to extreme cold, pressure and vacuum. It suffers no ill effects from being in deep ocean or planar space.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
trait.text: The World Serpent has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Thick Scales
trait.text: Whenever the World Serpent would take damage, it takes 10 less damage.

trait.name: Titanic Coil
trait.text: The World Serpent occupies a 30-foot-by-30-foot space and can coil into confined areas without squeezing. It ignores difficult terrain.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The World Serpent uses its Frightful Presence and then makes four attacks, one with its bite, two with its thrashes, and one with its tail, or it uses three actions that require a recharge.

action.name: Bite
action.text:
Melee Weapon Attack: +17 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. Hit: 43 (5d12+10) piercing damage plus 22 (5d8) poison damage. A large or smaller creature reduced to 0 hit points by this attack is swallowed by the World Serpent. While swallowed, the creature is unconscious and has total cover from effects outside the Serpent.
	At the start of each of the Serpent's turns, the swallowed creature takes 42 (12d6) acid damage from its digestive fluids. If the creature takes damage equal to or exceeding its hit point maximum while swallowed, its body is dissolved and cannot be revived by anything short of a true resurrection, wish, or similarly-powerful magic.
	If the World Serpent takes 50 or more damage in a single turn from a creature inside it, it must succeed on a DC 20 Constitution saving throw at the end of that turn or regurgitate all swallowed creatures, which fall prone in an unoccupied space within 10 feet of it.

action.name: Thresh
action.text: All creatures within 15 feet of the world serpent must succeed on a DC 24 Dexterity saving throw or take 23 (2d12+10) bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Tail
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +17 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. Hit: 27 (3d10+10) bludgeoning damage. Creatures damaged by this attack must succeed on a DC 24 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone.

action.name: Frightful Presence
action.text: Each creature of the World Serpent's choice within 120 ft. of it must succeed on a DC 16 Wisdom saving throw or become frightened for 1 minute. A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, with disadvantage if the World Serpent is within line of sight, ending the effect on itself on a success. If a creature's saving throw is successful or the effect ends for it, the creature is immune to the World Serpent's Frightful Presence for the next 24 hours.

action.name: Breaking Earth
action.text: The ground shudders and separates creating a deep fissure. All creatures in a 60 ft. line originating from the World Serpent must succeed on a DC 24 Dexterity saving throw or fall 20 ft. into the fissure, taking 9 (2d8) bludgeoning damage. Any creatures still in the fissure at the beginning of the World Serpent's next turn take 36 (8d8) bludgeoning damage and must succeed on a DC 24 Strength saving throw or become buried alive and begin suffocating. Creatures buried under rubble may free themselves as an action with a successful DC 22 Strength (Athletics) check.

action.name: Crashing Skies
action.text: The sky thunders. All creatures within 120 ft. of the World Serpent must make a DC 24 Dexterity saving throw, taking 21 (6d6) lightning damage on a failure or half as much on a success. Additionally, all airborne creatures within 500 ft. of the World Serpent must succeed on a DC 24 Strength saving throw or immediately fall 500 ft., taking the appropriate fall damage if they hit the ground.

action.name: Boiling Seas
action.text: The waters roil. All creatures within 120 ft. of the World Serpent must succeed on aa DC 24 Wisdom saving throw or take 33 (6d10) fire damage and make a second DC 24 Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, all liquids on their person, including potions, boil and disappear. Any creatures submerged in water has disadvantage on these saving throws.

action.name: Shattering Reality
action.text: The barrier between worlds breaks. All creatures within 60 ft. of the World Serpent must succeed on a DC 24 Intelligence saving throw or ascend 100 ft. floating weightless in the air., Any creature that failed this saving throw must make a second DC 24 Intelligence saving throw. On a failure, all magic items with charges in their possession lose one charge, and if they have any spell slots, they lose a spell slot of their choice. The weightlessness effect ends at the beginning of the World Serpent's next turn.

action.name: Doomsday
action.text:
Doomsday begins without a charge and a recharge action must be succeeded to use this action. All creatures within 120 ft. of the World Serpent must make a DC 24 Charisma saving throw. ON a failure, they take 13 (2d12) necrotic damage and 13 (2d12) radiant damage, and the creature's hit point maximum is reduced by this amount until greater restoration is cast on them. All creatures that failed this saving throw must make another DC 24 Charisma saving throw. On a failure, they are affliced with the Doomsady Curse.

Doomsday Curse - Bearers of this curse have -2 to all attack rolls, saving throws and ability checks. Multiple applications of this curse are cumulative.

legendary.name: Legendary Actions (3/Turn)
legendary.text: The dragon can take 3 legendary actions, choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature's turn. The dragon regains spent legendary actions at the start of its turn.

legendary.name: Bite
legendary.text: The World Serpent makes a single bite attack.

legendary.name: Move
legendary.text: The world serpent moves up to half its speed.

legendary.name: Spray Poison (Costs 3 Actions)
legendary.text: All creatures in a 90 ft. cone originating from the World Serpent must succeed on a DC 24 Constitution saving throw or take 26 (4d12) poison damage.

fields.description:
The World Serpent is a gargantuan, ancient monstrosity said to encircle the edges of the mortal world, its breath poisoning the sea and its coils shaking the earth. It speaks no language, yet its presence alone heralds omens, madness and the slow unravelling of order. Worshipped, feared or hunted by the gods, the World Serpent is all inevitability given ultimate form.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly - Legends of Norse Mythology p. 32 (Third Party)

fields.name: Cultist Initiate

trait.name: Obscure Devotion
trait.text: Gains advantage on saving throws against being frightened if within 15 ft. of a cult leader.

action.name: Dagger
action.text: Melee or Ranged Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5ft or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 1) piercing damage.

trait.text: Gains advantage on saving throws against beingfrightened if within 15 ft. of a cult leader.

action.name: Spellcasting
action.text:
The fanatic a 2nd-level spellcaster. Its spellcasting ability is Charisma (spell save DC 12, +4 to hit with spell attacks). It has the following spells prepared:

	• Cantrips (at will): Thaumaturgy, Sacred Flame.
	• 1st Level (3 slots): Command, Inflict Wounds

action.text: Melee weapon attack. +4 to hit. Reach 5 ft. One target. Hit: 5 (1d6+2) piercing damage.

trait.name: Spellcasting
trait.text:
The heirophant is a 6th-level spellcaster. Its spellcasting ability is Charisma (Spell save DC 15, +7 to hit).

	• Cantrips (at will): Thaumaturgy, Prestidigitation, Toll the Dead
	• 1st Level (4 slots): Charm Person, Command, Shield of Faith
	• 2nd level (3 slots): Hold Person, Mirror Image, Bestow Curse, Suggestion

trait.name: Will of the Patron
trait.text: Cult allies within 10 ft. of the hierophant can't be charmed or frightened unless the hierophant is incapacitated.

action.name: Staff
action.text: Melee weapon attack: +4 to hit. Reach 5 ft. One taraget. Hit: 5 (1d6+1) bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Soulflare
action.text: One creature the hierophant can see within 60 ft. must make a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw or take 21 (6d6) psychic damage and be stunned until the end of its next turn.

fields.name: Death Cultist

trait.name: Bloodletting Slash
trait.text: The cultist deals an extra 5 (1d8) necrotic damage when it deals damage to a creature that is frightened or charmed.

trait.name: Final Rites
trait.text: When the death cultist is reduced to 0 hit points, all creatures within 5 ft. must succeed on a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw or be frightened until the end of their turn.

action.name: Dagger
action.text: Melee weapon attack: +4 to hit, reach 5ft, one target. Hit: 7 (1d6+3) piercing damage plus 5 (1d8) necrotic damage if the target is frightened or charmed.

action.name: Morbid Fascination
action.text: One creature the death cultist can see within 60 ft. must attempt a DC 13 Charisma saving throw. ON a failure, the creature is frightened of the death cultist until the end of their next turn. On a success, the creature is charmed by the death cultist until the end of their next turn.

action.name: Necrotic Pulse
action.text: The cultist exhales a wave of shadow in a 15-foot cone. Each creature in the area must make a DC 13 Constitution saving throw, taking 11 (3d6) necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much on a success.

fields.description: Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly (Sinister Cult) p. 20 (Third Party)

fields.name: Elemental Cultist (Water)

trait.name: Tide's Grasp
trait.text: Creatures that start their turn in water conjured by the water cultist must succeed on a DC 13 Strength saving throw or fall prone.

trait.name: Spellcasting
trait.text:
The cultist is a 3rd-level spellcaster. Its spellcasting ability is Wisdom (spell save DC 12, +4 to hit with spell attacks).

	• Cantrips (at will): Thaumaturgy, Frostbite, Shape Water
	• 1st Level (4 slots): Create or Destroy Water, Command
	• 2nd Level (2 slots): Hold Person, Mirror Image

action.name: Staff
action.text: Melee weapon attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. Hit: 5 (1d6+1) bludgeoning damage plus 3 (1d4) cold damage.

action.name: Chilling Tide
action.text: The cultist unleashes a wave of freezing brine in a 15-foot cone. Each creature in the area must make a DC 13 Constitution saving throw. On a failed saving throw creatures take 14 (3d8) cold damage and their movement is halved until the start of the cultist's next turn. Characters take half damage and do not lose their speed as much on a successful saving throw.

trait.name: Ashen Rebirth
trait.text: When the cultist is reduced to 0 hit points, it erupts in a blaze. Each creature within 10 ft. must succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw or take 7 (2d6) fire damage, taking half damage on a success.

trait.name: Spellcasting
trait.text:
The cultist is a 3rd-level spellcaster. Its spellcasting ability is Charisma (spell save DC 12, +4 to hit with spell attacked). It requires no material components.

	• Cantrips (at will): Produce Flame, Thaumaturgy
	• 1st Level (4 slots): Burning Hands, Hellish Rebuke

action.name: Mace

fields.name: Elemental Cultist (Wind)

trait.name: Wind Walker
trait.text: The cultist has advantage on saving throws against effects that would cause it to be restrained or grappled.

action.name: Handaxe
action.text: Melee weapon attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d6+3) slashing damage plus 3 (1d4) thunder damage.

action.name: Shrieking Gale
action.text: The cultist conjures a burst of violent wind in a 15-foot cone. Each creature in the area must succeed on a DC 13 Strength saving throw or be pushed 10 ft. away and knocked prone. Objects and flames in the area are extinguished or blown aside.

action.name: Gale Dash (Bonus Action)
action.text: As a bonus action, the cultist can move 15 ft. without provoking opportunity attacks.

fields.description: Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly (Sinister Cult) p. 23 (Third Party)

trait.name: Galvanic Grip
trait.text: The cultist has advantage on saving throws against being knocked prone or moved against its will.

action.name: Maul
action.text: Melee weapon attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., Hit: 9 (2d6+2) bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Earth Tremor
action.text: The cultist causes a tremor in the ground centered around them in a 10-foot radius. Each creature other than the cultist in the area must make a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw or take 6 (1d10) bludgeoning damage and be knocked prone. The area becomes difficult terrain.

reaction.name: Earthen Fortitude
reaction.text: When the earth cultist takes bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage from a non-magical weapon, they can use their reaction to reduce the damage by 5.

fields.description: Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly (Sinister Cult) p. 24 (Third Party)

trait.name: Hellbound Reinforcements
trait.text: Once per day, the cultists can cast Spirit Guardians without using a spell slot.

action.name: Spellcasting

The cultist is a 6th-level spellcaster. Its spellcasting ability is Charisma (Spell save DC 14, +6 to hit with spell attacks). It does not require material components.

	• Cantrips (at will): Thaumaturgy, Fire Bolt, Minor Illusion

action.name: Pact Sigil (Bonus Action)
action.text: The cultist marks a creature they can see within 60 ft. The marked creature gains 10 temporary hit points. If the marked creature dies before the end of the cultist's next turn, the cultist regains an expended spell slot of 2nd level or lower.

action.text: The agog makes a Bite attack against a Prone target.

fields.description:
This horrific thing has no shape or body resembling anything from the Mortal World. It roughly resembles a tree stump with four root-like legs each ending in a misshapen hoof. It has a wet, mottled, bark-like hide, and sprouting from the side of it like branches are knobbly arms ending in sharp claws. The top of its body is a gaping, tooth-filled mouth. It is shovelling chunks of horse-flesh into itself, and giggling as it swallows the ripped flesh. Whatever passes for arms, on the inside of the palm are yellow eyes.

Study the Foe:
Characters proficient in History or Nature gain Advantage on Intelligence (Arcana) checks when they take the Study action to examine an Agog, learning the following based on the result.
(5+) Climbing Aberration. You know the creature's type, and movement speeds.
(10+) Attack the Fallen. You are aware of the creature's Gobble Bonus Action.
(15+) Dim but Sturdy. You recognize the creature's highest and lowest ability scores.

Combat Tactics:
The Agog barrels towards its enemies, flailing its arms towards them and attempting to grab them and toss them to the ground. If it knocks a creature down, it will immediately begin attempting to devour them.

Source:	Sebastian Crowes Terror in Tierhaven p. 18 (Third Party),
		Pluto Jackson's Monsters of Drakkenheim p. 292 (Third Party)

This creature has gaunt and misshapen form, with the scaled body, tail, and head of an alligator, bony spokes covering its body like a porcupine, batlike wings, and long, spindly limbs.

Study the Foe:
Characters proficient in History or Nature gain Advantage on Intelligence (Arcana) checks when they take the Study action to examine an Allopine, learning the following based on the result.
(5+) Flying Aberration. You know the creature's type, and movement speeds.
(10+) Shifty. You are aware of the creature's Nimble Escape Bonus Action.
(15+) Agile but Meek. They learn the creature's highest and lowest ability scores.

Allopines are not warriors, but they are hostile to creatures who enter their territory and will fire Quills at anyone who comes too close. They do not stick around in a fight by themselves, and if they are with a flock, they will prefer to take to the air and fire Quills from afar.

The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

action.text: Each creature of the archlich's choice within 120 feet of it and aware of it must succeed on a DC 20 Wisdom saving throw or become frightened for 1 minute. A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, with disadvantage if the archlich is within line of sight, ending the effect on itself on a success. If a creature's saving throw is successful or the effect ends for it, the creature is immune to the archlich's Frightful Presence for the next 24 hours.

legendary.name: Legendary Actions (3/Turn)
legendary.text: The archlich can take 3 legendary actions, choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature's turn. The archlich regains spent legendary actions at the start of its turn.

legendary.name: Paralyzing Touch
legendary.text: The archlich uses its Paralyzing Touch.

legendary.name: Sacrifice
legendary.text: The archlich reduces an undead under its control to 0 hit points, and regains 2d10 + 20 hit points.

legendary.name: Disrupt Life (Costs 2 Actions)
legendary.text: Each living creature within 20 feet of the archlich must make a DC 20 Constitution saving throw against this magic, taking 54 (12d8) necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

legendary.name: An Archlich's Lair
legendary.text:
If an archlich were to escape its prison, it would be able to create a lair for itself fairly quickly. Using the armies of undead it easily amasses, an archlich can build great castles and towers for itself, designing grand halls, mighty defenses, and cunning traps meant to ward off all intrusion.
	An archlich's lair would be filled with strategically placed undead, meant to emerge and surround unlucky visitors. The lair would also include a residence for those that have made a pact with the archlich, both to keep those allies in good standing and to help protect the lair.
	An archlich encountered in its lair has a challenge rating of 31 (175,000 XP).

legendary.name:
Lair Actions
on Initiative Count 20 (Losing Initiative Ties), the Archlich Can Take
a Lair Action to Cause One of the Following Magical Effects; the Lich
can't Use the Same Effect Two Rounds in a Row
legendary.text:
On initiative count 20 (losing initiative ties), the archlich can take a lair action to cause one of the following magical effects; the lich can't use the same effect two rounds in a row:

	• The archlich rolls 2d8 and takes the higher roll, regaining a spell slot of the level rolled or lower. If it has no spent spell slots of that level or lower, nothing happens.

	• The archlich targets one creature it can see within 30 feet of it. A crackling cord of negative energy tethers thelich to the target. Whenever the lich takes damage, the target must make a DC 20 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the lich takes half the damage (rounded down), and the target takes the remaining damage. This tether lasts until initiative count 20 on the next round or until the lich or the target is no longer in the lich's lair.

	• The lich calls forth the spirits of creatures that died in its lair. These apparitions materialize and attack one creature that the lich can see within 60 feet of it. The target must succeed on a DC 20 Constitution saving throw, becoming paralyzed for 1 minute and taking 52 (15d6) necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a success. The apparitions then disappear. A paralyzed creature can repeat the saving throw at the start of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

fields.description:
Archliches are beings of immense magical power outmatched by only the gods themselves. Through their many millennia of existence, archliches have mastered all arts of necromancy. But these beings are still not satisfied with their near limitless power — they still yearn for more, and they hunger for even greater arcane knowledge. Supremely intelligent, these creatures enact schemes that last for hundreds of years — which is just a blip in their unending existence.
	An archlich appears almost completely skeletal, with only a few wisps of flesh and hair left on its frame. The lights of their eyes disappeared long ago, so all that remains are black, empty sockets. They choose to adorn themselves with kingly attire, believing themselves to be the rightful rulers of the land.

	Dark Creation. Archliches are the oldest beings known to exist, originally and only created during the Crown Wars over ten thousand years ago. Long tired of the unending war, a few elves yearned to gain the power that would allow them end the war themselves. So these few became high mages, sages with unmatched magical power for their time. But they still needed more, as this war couldn't be ended with normal magic in the span of a single mortal life.
	So these mages devoted their entire lives to the study of necromancy, and learned the secrets to lichdom from their dealings with the dark gods of the time. These gods gave them the forbidden knowledge needed to ascend past even the most powerful liches, which hasn't been given to a mortal mind before or since. Using this knowledge, these mages began the arcane ritual. This ritual released a huge storm of necrotic power onto the world; an event now known as the Dark Disaster.
	The Dark Disaster destroyed an entire elvish kingdom, and reduced the surrounding area to a barren wasteland. This power also proved too much for the minds of the mages, and they lost all memory of their original purpose and their mortal life, but they had gained the power they had so desired.

	Enemy of the Gods. Once the gods saw the destruction wrought by the Dark Disaster, they knew they needed to intervene. Celestial agents were sent to destroy these few archliches, but even the most powerful of angels couldn't fully destroy them. But eventually, after only a few months of destruction, all the archliches were banished to other planes, supposedly to never be seen again.
	After they were all dispatched, the gods sought to never allow another mortal to ascend to that degree of lichdom again. They used all their power to hide that forbidden knowledge, and even convinced some of the most evil deities to never to part with the knowledge.

	Pact-makers. Although all the archliches were banished and trapped in their own demiplanes, a few of them have learned how to contact mortals in the material plane, though as of yet none have escaped the confines of their prison. By gaining mortal followers, an archlich hopes to free itself and become a ruler of the mortal world.
	Those that are make a pact with an archlich are granted a degree of magical power, with the assumption that they will serve and put all their resources towards freeing their master. They believe that with the outside influence gained through these pacts, they will eventually find a creature capable of freeing them and inflicting them upon the world.

	Death and Restoration. An archlich's phylactery is located within its demiplane, and is completely indestructible and inaccessible to all but the archlich. However, this means that if an archlich were to escape from their confines and then allow their body to be destroyed, they would once again be trapped within the demiplane when their body reforms.
	Since an archlich requires the assistance of powerful spell casters to return to the material plane, it is necessary for them to attempt to create and hold allegiances with mortals. If a mortal was to learn how to summon an archlich from their plane of existence, the archlich would be obligated to keep that mortal alive and allied, for the archlich may need that mortal again if their body is destroyed and they are restored to their plane.

	Undead Nature. An archlich doesn't require air, food, drink or sleep.

Source:	Dark Arts Player's Companion p. 32 (Homebrew)

fields.description:
Bloodbeasts roam destroyed forests and barren plains, searching for signs of life that signal the presence of their prey. These savage creatures scour the landscape for small towns and dens, snatching and devouring any residents that they find. Their victims are often found days later, drained of all their blood.
	Bloodbeasts take the form of thin, decrepit dire wolves, with crimson-hued fur and pale pink skin. Although these beasts look to be in ill health at first glance, the magic that runs through their veins makes them a powerful foe to face.

	Beasts of Yeenoghu. When a hyena feasts on a creature slain by a gnoll fang of Yeenoghu, that hyena undergoes a horrid transformation into a gnoll. However, there is also another lesser known, unintended transformation: the creation of bloodbeasts. When a dire wolf eats a creature that has been slain in that way, it instead undergoes a transformation into a bloodbeast, a creature imbued with the savagery and insatiable hunger of Yeenoghu himself. This process is extremely rare, since the territories of gnolls and dire wolves rarely intersect. But when they do, these powerful beasts can wreak havoc among the small packs of gnolls that dot the barren landscapes these beasts call home.

	Lone Hunters. When a bloodbeast is created, it quickly disappears from the scene of its creation and hides from the gnolls that accidentally brought it into existence. It is only after a few days that the beast is ready to venture out and search for its prey. Bloodbeasts stalk the landscape in the dead of night, searching for weak creatures that they can easily ambush and quickly kill. After becoming a blood beast, these creatures no longer have any desire to procreate or work in packs.

	Enemy of the Gnolls. Larger groups of gnolls that see a bloodbeast will kill it on sight, knowing that these creatures can easily pick off all but the most powerful gnolls in one-on-one combat.

Source:	Dark Arts Player's Companion p. 34 (Homebrew)
